openings.claim: Connect load-state tags with confirmed requested windows: removal updates reveal release; anonymous confirmation distinguishes intentions from arrivals. Together they may reduce searches.
openings.discriminator: Current combined records outperform updated tags alone and confirmed windows alone.
openings.probe: Compare all three conditions under equal arrival schedules; measure search and per-load recording time. Stop if recording exceeds one minute or identities are required.
openings.uncertainty: Untested. Depends on residents updating removal state and quick anonymous confirmation. Prompt tag removal, calendar influence on arrivals and drying-duration variability remain unknown.

openings.claim: Removing an empty hanger’s tag together with a visible vacancy marker may make released capacity easier to identify by representing vacancy explicitly.
openings.discriminator: Paired changes outperform tag removal alone when visual ambiguity causes searches.
openings.probe: Compare paired changes, tag removal alone and existing practice. Stop if markers obscure occupied laundry or require moving another load.
openings.uncertainty: No effect established. Depends on released spaces being hard to distinguish and markers fitting existing racks.

lineage.reason: Preserves the connection between two records and the comparison against either alone.
Preserves paired tag removal and explicit vacancy signaling, including the tag-removal comparator.

decision: Retain both as untested hypotheses. All supplied observations are synthetic stipulations. Preserve four racks and room layout; never move another resident’s laundry; keep per-load recording within one minute; record no names or apartment numbers. Judge success during the stipulated busy period: at least nine of ten arrivals find usable space within three minutes without moving another load.
